methodology.heading: Methodology
methodology.sentence1: For us, every challenge revolves around people.

folders.title: E6 Repair Coalition
folders.challenge: The municipality needed insight into the fragmented electronic repair sector and support in building a coalition around repair, circular economy and local collaboration.
folders.solution: JCP conducted a deep sector analysis, mapped repair actors across The Hague, identified strategic coalition partners, and developed an approach for organising and activating the sector. This included stakeholder sessions, mobilisation strategies and coalition building around shared ambitions for repair and circularity.
folders.description: As part of a European circular economy trajectory, JCP supported the development of a local repair ecosystem focused on electronic and household device repair. The project combined research, stakeholder engagement and coalition building to strengthen collaboration between repair shops, educational institutions, community initiatives and public actors. By translating a fragmented landscape into a shared network and direction, the project helped lay the foundation for a more visible, accessible and future proof repair sector in The Hague.
services: Strategy development for circular economy activation

folders.title: ESPON – Urban Circular Collaborative Economy
folders.challenge: A European consortium led by the City of The Hague wanted to better understand how urban circular and collaborative economy initiatives operate across Europe, and how cities could learn from emerging sharing economy models.
folders.solution: JCP initiated, developed and led the project for the municipality of The Hague, coordinating research, stakeholder collaboration and international exchange within the ESPON programme.
folders.description: Within the European ESPON programme, JCP helped establish and lead an international research and collaboration project focused on the urban circular collaborative economy. The project explored how cities across Europe are experimenting with sharing systems, and community based economic models. By connecting policy, research and local practice, the project contributed to new insights into how cities can support more resilient and regenerative urban economies.

folders.title: URBACT – Resourceful Cities
folders.challenge: The City of The Hague aimed to strengthen its approach to urban resource management and circularity while learning from other European cities facing similar challenges.
folders.solution: JCP helped initiate, shape and lead the URBACT Resourceful Cities trajectory for the municipality, coordinating local stakeholder engagement, international exchange and strategic development around circular urban systems.
folders.description: Through the URBACT Resourceful Cities network, JCP supported the City of The Hague in developing new approaches to urban circularity, resource use and local collaboration. The project connected European cities around shared questions related to waste, reuse, local production and community driven sustainability. JCP played a central role in translating international knowledge into local strategies and stakeholder processes that strengthened collaboration between institutions, residents and practitioners.

about.heading: About Us
about.heroSubtitle: We support European municipalities and B2B organisations in translating sustainability policy into structured governance, measurable outcomes, and operational implementation.
about.whoTitle: Independent ESG advisory for complex public environments.
about.whoBody: We are a small, expert-led consultancy specialising in sustainability strategy, governance alignment, and regulatory implementation across the Netherlands and neighbouring European markets. We work with municipalities and private-sector organisations operating in regulated, multi-stakeholder environments. Our role is to structure ESG ambition into coherent frameworks that withstand public scrutiny, regulatory review, and operational reality. Sustainability in public contexts demands precision. We bring that structure.
about.contextBody: The European regulatory environment is evolving rapidly — from the European Green Deal to CSRD reporting obligations and taxonomy alignment. Municipalities face increasing expectations around transparency, climate adaptation, procurement sustainability, and measurable impact. We help organisations interpret these requirements pragmatically and embed them into governance, reporting, and operational systems.

approachSteps.title: 01 — Regulatory & policy mapping
approachSteps.body: We analyse applicable EU and national frameworks, local policy ambitions, and stakeholder expectations.

approachSteps.title: 02 — Double materiality & risk assessment
approachSteps.body: We identify material ESG factors and translate them into actionable priorities.

approachSteps.title: 03 — Governance & operational alignment
approachSteps.body: We integrate ESG objectives into procurement processes, internal controls, reporting structures, and cross-departmental workflows.

approachSteps.title: 04 — Monitoring & reporting systems
approachSteps.body: We establish measurable KPIs and reporting structures aligned with European regulatory standards.
